<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.

Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Some models use the same architecture name in SGLang but need different mono kernel specs. For example, dsv4-pro and dsv41 both run as `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. The mono kernel registry looks up a spec by architecture only, so it cannot tell these two models apart.

This PR lets the registry also use the model type (`model_type` in the model's config) to choose the spec.

Needed by sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#48. Merge this PR before it.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Registering (plugin side): `register()` in `kernels/plugin_kernels/amd/spec.py` takes an optional `model_type`. A plugin can register a spec for one model type, or leave `model_type` out (`None`).
- Looking up (sglang side): Sglang's startup check and runtime in `srt/kernel_plugins/amd/binding.py` pass the served model's `hf_config.model_type` to `find_spec()` and `spec_registered()`. A lookup first tries a spec registered for that model type, then a spec registered without one.

With the current sgl-amd-mono repo, every model gets the same spec with and without this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

None.

- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -170,29 +170,55 @@ def widths(self, isa: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
         return self.devices[isa].widths
 
 
-# backend name -> HF architecture -> the "module:attribute" path of its spec
-_REGISTRY: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
-
-
-def register(*, backend: str, architecture: str, path: str) -> None:
-    """Register a module:attribute spec path from a general plugin entry point."""
+# backend name -> (HF architecture, model type or None) -> the "module:attribute"
+# path of its spec
+_REGISTRY: dict[str, dict[tuple[str, Optional[str]], str]] = {}
+
+
+def register(
+    *, backend: str, architecture: str, path: str, model_type: Optional[str] = None
+) -> None:
+    """Register a module:attribute spec path from a general plugin entry point. A
+    spec registered with a ``model_type`` serves only configs of that model type, and
+    is looked up before one registered for the architecture alone: models that share
+    an architecture (DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1) can each have their own."""
     specs = _REGISTRY.setdefault(backend, {})
-    if specs.get(architecture, path) != path:
+    key = (architecture, model_type)
+    if specs.get(key, path) != path:
+        of = architecture if model_type is None else f"{architecture} ({model_type})"
         raise ValueError(
-            f"monokernel backend {backend!r} already has a spec for {architecture}: "
-            f"{specs[architecture]}"
+            f"monokernel backend {backend!r} already has a spec for {of}: {specs[key]}"
         )
-    specs[architecture] = path
+    specs[key] = path
+
 
+def _spec_path(
+    specs: dict[tuple[str, Optional[str]], str],
+    architecture: str,
+    model_type: Optional[str],
+) -> Optional[str]:
+    return specs.get((architecture, model_type)) or specs.get((architecture, None))
 
-def spec_registered(*, backend: str, architectures: Optional[Sequence[str]]) -> bool:
+
+def spec_registered(
+    *,
+    backend: str,
+    architectures: Optional[Sequence[str]],
+    model_type: Optional[str] = None,
+) -> bool:
     """Whether the backend registers a spec for any architecture, usable or not."""
     specs = _REGISTRY.get(backend, {})
-    return any(arch in specs for arch in architectures or ())
+    return any(
+        _spec_path(specs, arch, model_type) is not None for arch in architectures or ()
+    )
 
 
 def find_spec(
-    *, backend: str, architectures: Optional[Sequence[str]], isa: Optional[str]
+    *,
+    backend: str,
+    architectures: Optional[Sequence[str]],
+    isa: Optional[str],
+    model_type: Optional[str] = None,
 ) -> tuple[Optional[MonoSpec], str]:
     """The compatible spec and an empty reason, or None and a rejection reason."""
     if backend not in _REGISTRY:
@@ -202,7 +228,7 @@ def find_spec(
         )
     why = []
     for arch in architectures or ():
-        path = _REGISTRY[backend].get(arch)
+        path = _spec_path(_REGISTRY[backend], arch, model_type)
         if path is None:
             continue
         module, _, attr = path.partition(":")

@@ -135,7 +135,10 @@ def monokernel_disable_reasons(
         return None, ["no GPU is visible"]
     hf_config = model_config.hf_config
     spec, why = find_spec(
-        backend=BACKEND, architectures=hf_config.architectures, isa=isa
+        backend=BACKEND,
+        architectures=hf_config.architectures,
+        isa=isa,
+        model_type=getattr(hf_config, "model_type", None),
     )
     if spec is None:
         return None, [why]
@@ -274,7 +277,10 @@ def monokernel_weights_iterator(
     if backend is None:
         return weights
     spec, _ = find_spec(
-        backend=backend, architectures=model.config.architectures, isa=device_isa()
+        backend=backend,
+        architectures=model.config.architectures,
+        isa=device_isa(),
+        model_type=getattr(model.config, "model_type", None),
     )
     if spec is None or spec.load_tensor is None:
         return weights
@@ -324,14 +330,19 @@ def install_monokernel_forward(
         return
     isa = device_isa()
     archs = hf_config.architectures
-    spec, why = find_spec(backend=backend, architectures=archs, isa=isa)
+    model_type = getattr(hf_config, "model_type", None)
+    spec, why = find_spec(
+        backend=backend, architectures=archs, isa=isa, model_type=model_type
+    )
     is_load_observed = "_mono_copies" in model.__dict__
     copies = model.__dict__.pop("_mono_copies", {})
     # Ranks branch together; one skipping the collectives below would hang its peers.
     lookups = _gather_tp(
         (
             spec is not None,
-            spec_registered(backend=backend, architectures=archs),
+            spec_registered(
+                backend=backend, architectures=archs, model_type=model_type
+            ),
             why,
             None if spec is None else (spec.name, spec.api_version),
         )
